title: Zero-twisted lift contributes one to the Fourier sum
statement:
Fix an integer $k \ge 1$, and let $f : \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{Z}_k$ be arbitrary. Write $\widetilde{f}_0(x) = \omega_k^{\,0 \cdot f(x)}$ for the $0$-twisted lift of $f$ (equivalently, the constant function $1$), and let $\widehat{\widetilde{f}_0}(s)$ denote its Fourier coefficient at frequency $s \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n$. Then
\[
  \sum_{s \in \mathbb{Z}_k^n}
    \bigl|\widehat{\widetilde{f}_0}(s)\bigr|^2 \,
    \operatorname{Re}\widehat{\widetilde{f}_0}(s) = 1,
\]
where $|\cdot|$ is the complex modulus.
hypotheses_covered: f is an arbitrary function from ℤ_k^n to ℤ_k
replaced:
For any $f : \mathbb{Z}_k^n \to \mathbb{Z}_k$, the $j=0$ term of the Fourier
sum evaluates to $1$:
\[
  \sum_{s\in\mathbb{Z}_k^n}
  \bigl\|\widehat{(\widetilde{f}_0)}(s)\bigr\|^2\,
  \operatorname{Re}\!\left[\widehat{(\widetilde{f}_0)}(s)\right] = 1.
\]
